title: Breaking the Human Review Bottleneck: Can LLM-Generated Proof Summaries Replace Line-by-Line Review?

original_idea.body:
# Breaking the Human Review Bottleneck: Can LLM-Generated Proof Summaries Replace Line-by-Line Review?

**Problem:** Human review of Lean 4 proofs is the primary bottleneck in deploying formally verified AI-generated code. Whether natural language proof summaries generated by LLMs are sufficient for human review is unstudied.

**Direction:** Take 30 complete Lean 4 proofs. Have LLMs generate natural language summaries. Ask 10 CS students to: (a) approve/reject based on summary only, (b) approve/reject after reading full proof. Measure false approval rate per condition. Test whether summary-based review catches the same errors as full-proof review.

**Why it matters:** If LLM-generated summaries enable equally accurate human review in 10% of the time, the practical deployment bottleneck for formally verified AI code would be dramatically reduced.

**Relevant context:** Claude Code Security uses multi-stage verification to reduce false positives. Human review of formal proofs is mentioned as a bottleneck in multiple papers. The summary-as-review approach is unexplored.
